content:
Hi everyone! I'm Jianan Yao, an assistant professor at the University of Toronto working on formal verification of systems software.

My research group is considering building a Rust-to-Lean transpiler on top of Iris-Lean. We're interested in drawing on ideas from RefinedRust, a Rust-to-Rocq verification tool built on Iris-Rocq.

The motivation is to support verification involving heap memory, raw pointers, and fine-grained concurrency. Aeneas, an existing Rust verification toolchain with a Lean backend, translates Rust into a pure functional representation, which does not directly support the memory-level reasoning we need for low-level software. We think Iris-Lean could provide a good foundation for a different approach.

Before pursuing this further, I wanted to ask whether anyone in the Iris-Lean community is already working on, or planning, a Rust verification tool or a similar application. We'd like to avoid duplicating ongoing work and would be happy to coordinate if there's overlap.

Thanks!
I do plan to start porting lambda-rust, but do not have time right now.

Thanks for the heads-up! Given your current bandwidth constraints, I guess our team can start exploring the Rust-to-Lean verification toolchain. We'd be happy to discuss potential coordination or collaboration with your lambda-rust port down the road.
Awesome! Glad to hear somebody is working on this now--if you run into any issues with the framework don't hesitate to reach out :)

Thanks, Markus! I had one question about the Iris-Lean paper's mention of integration with CSLib. What kind of integration does the team have in mind? Is it mainly about reusing the foundations in Pillar 1, such as common data structures and formalized programming-language concepts, or are you also considering a closer integration with Pillar 2 (Boole), for example, connecting Iris-Lean with Boole's verification-condition generation infrastructure? Or is the direction still open?

I'm trying to understand how Iris-Lean might fit into the broader Lean verification ecosystem as we think about the architecture and dependencies of our Rust-to-Lean transpiler. I'd greatly appreciate your thoughts.

I think it would be nice to at least make a language instance for the languages in CSLib, and for Boole, if for no other reason that to help canonicalize the story for program verification in Lean. One thing that might also be interesting would be to try using the completeness results for Iris (which we also ported) to lift facts proven classically or opaquely using Boole's infrastructure as Iris proofs. I've sort of done that second bit for mvcgen, I meant to write a blog post about it but it slipped my mind, oops!

Tighter connections, such as reusing vc generators, is not something I've spent a lot of time thinking about yet. Partly, because it seems that agents + Iris serve as very good vc generators, so we can get a lot out of just making Iris faster. If however "an Iris logic (or Language instance) for all Boole languages" is something you end up prototyping we could spend some time integrating that into the library too!
This is just my two cents, anyways. The others should chime in if they have different thoughts :)

Thanks, Markus! This is very helpful. I think we'll start by building the Rust-to-Lean transpiler directly on Iris-Lean, rather than going through Boole. Since we want to support raw pointers and fine-grained concurrency, depending on Boole would introduce too much uncertainty and scope for the initial project, given that its development is outside our control and its current first-order VC-based approach doesn't yet support the reasoning we need.

We'll try to keep the implementation modular so that we can take advantage of future integration between Iris-Lean and CSLib as the ecosystem evolves. Thanks again for the insights and for the offer to help with integration!

Hi Jianan, this sounds like a cool project and I am also not aware of someone working on Rust verification based on Iris Lean at this point.
If you are interested in defining the semantics of a complex language like Rust, you might be interested in the Program Logics a la carte approach for defining language semantics. There is a port of this approach to Lean here. (It is at this point a bit WIP, but hopefully will be pushed over the finishing line soon.)
Also if you are interested in taking ideas for RefinedRust, you might be interested in the Lithium proof automation that underlies RefinedRust. If this is the case, please let me know since I also have a WIP port of Lithium to Lean. Maybe these pointers are useful.

There is https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.04372 Corten, which combines Hax with iris.
I have WIP on a partially verified Hax backend in lean (https://github.com/spitters/hax-lean). It prints to a number of imperative languages.
Targeting iris is possible too.

Jianan Yao said:

Before pursuing this further, I wanted to ask whether anyone in the Iris-Lean community is already working on, or planning, a Rust verification tool or a similar application.

Not sure if you're aware, but the Aeneas authors are also tackling this problem of translating unsafe Rust into Lean, and afaik they meant to use Iris Lean as well. Might be interesting to check up with them on their Zulip.

Complementing @Fernando LEAL's remark, @Jianan Yao we haven't communicated much about it but in case you're interested we've been extending Aeneas to add separation logic over the summer : the idea is to benefit from the pure translation whenever possible and resort to separation logic when necessary. We're doing it in several steps: we've made good progress on adding support for basic usages of raw pointers with first order separation logic (we plan to finish this work in the coming weeks) and are working on the memory model in parallel (to support transmute and pointer arithmetic for instance) together with a proper connection with iris-lean to reason about concurrency.

Thanks everyone for the pointers! I wasn't aware that the Aeneas team was already working on separation logic and an Iris-Lean integration. This overlaps quite a bit with what I had in mind.

@Son Ho, would you be open to chatting privately about your plans? I'd love to learn more and see if there might be room for collaboration.
Yes, let's do that: I sent you a PM.
